acceptance_criteria: Cascade destroy implemented. All descendant ids in destroyed list.
close_reason: Implemented onDestroyRemoveChildren cascade: get_descendant_ids, destroy each descendant, cascade failure reports parent in notDestroyed; +1 test; 19 total pass; clippy clean
description:
**What:** When onDestroyRemoveChildren=true and a node is destroyed, destroy all descendants and include their ids in the destroyed response. Oracle: §3.2.3 MUST include ids of all deleted nodes.

**Algorithm:**
1. When onDestroyRemoveChildren=true:
   a. Call get_descendant_ids for the node id.
   b. Call destroy_object for each descendant (leaf-first order preferred; flat order acceptable).
   c. On any descendant destroy error: insert serverFail for the top-level id in notDestroyed; continue.
   d. Push each descendant id to destroyed_list.
   e. Then call destroy_object for the top-level node.
2. When onDestroyRemoveChildren=false: use get_descendant_ids (from FA) for the nodeHasChildren guard — already updated in FA.
3. Update MockBackend: add set_descendants(node_id, [child_ids]) helper.

**Tests:**
- onDestroyRemoveChildren=true: all descendant ids appear in destroyed list. Oracle: §3.2.3.
- onDestroyRemoveChildren=true + descendant destroy fails: top-level in notDestroyed with serverFail.
- onDestroyRemoveChildren=false + node has children not in destroy set → nodeHasChildren. Already tested in FA.
- onDestroyRemoveChildren=false + leaf node → destroys normally.

**Acceptance criteria:** All tests pass. cargo test -p jmap-filenode-server exits 0.
title: Implement onDestroyRemoveChildren cascade in FileNode/set
